runtime: Rust standard library (rust-src); callbacks are typed with Fn* bounds, so no native rows are needed
conventions: Types: fn pointers, impl/dyn Fn*/AsyncFn* and type parameters bounded by them are function types (classified structurally); an unbounded type parameter or dyn Any is a top type. Box/Arc/Rc/Pin/Option are transparent wrappers.

io_send.describe: the C library's connect(fd, addr, len), reached from std::net through an extern "C" declaration without Rust source
the C library's execvp(file, argv), reached from std::process::Command through an extern "C" declaration
the C library's posix_spawnp(pid, file, ...), reached from std::process::Command through an extern "C" declaration
the Windows API CreateProcessW(application, command_line, ...), reached from std::process::Command on Windows

ffi_conventions.describe: a #[no_mangle] (or #[unsafe(no_mangle)]) extern function is exported under its own name to C and every language with a C FFI
the function is exported under the given symbol name
a foreign function declaration: calls go to the C symbol name (or #[link_name])
functions of this extern block are wasm imports from module m, provided by the host

test_conventions.describe: cargo test runs every function marked #[test] (also inside #[cfg(test)] modules); #[bench] under cargo bench
Cargo integration tests: each tests/*.rs file is a test crate (unless Cargo.toml [[test]] entries say otherwise)

syntax_conventions.describe: a #[pyfunction] is exported to Python under its name (or its name key); the procedural macro writes the binding glue at build time
a #[pyclass] struct / enum is a Python class under its name (or its name key)
every function of a #[pymethods] impl block is a method of the Python class
a #[pymodule] function is the extension module's init (PyInit_<name>); it registers functions and classes
#[pyo3(name = "x")] renames the exported function, class or method
the name = "x" key of the binding attributes is the Python-visible name
#[pyclass(module = "m")] names the Python module of the class
a #[new] method of a #[pymethods] block is the class's __new__ (calling the class runs it)
wrap_pyfunction!(f, m) inside a #[pymodule] registers f in that module
m.add_class::<T>() inside a #[pymodule] registers class T in that module
m.add_function(..) inside a #[pymodule] registers a function in that module
m.add_wrapped(..) inside a #[pymodule] registers a function in that module
a #[wasm_bindgen] function is a JavaScript export of the generated package under its name (or js_name)
a #[wasm_bindgen] struct / enum is a JavaScript class / object of the generated package
the pub functions of a #[wasm_bindgen] impl block are methods of the generated JavaScript class
the variants of a C-style #[wasm_bindgen] enum are properties of the generated JavaScript object (Cell.Alive)
js_name = x renames the JavaScript export
#[wasm_bindgen(constructor)] makes the method the JavaScript class constructor (new Class())
a #[wasm_bindgen] extern block imports JavaScript functions; its items are not C symbols
a #[napi] function is an export of the Node addon (camelCase name unless js_name)
a #[napi] struct / enum is a JavaScript class / object of the Node addon
the functions of a #[napi] impl block that carry #[napi] themselves are methods of the JavaScript class
js_name = "x" renames the JavaScript export
#[napi(constructor)] makes the method the JavaScript class constructor
#[napi(factory)] makes the method a JavaScript factory of the class
#[napi] exports snake_case functions and methods under their camelCase name
